collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 45 or older and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: A young villager asks how an older one came to be in charge of the canoes: tell the whole story, or make it short.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) is young and impatient and wants to know how (subject) ended up as the person in charge of the village's canoes. (subject) starts to explain. It takes a long time. First (subject.he/she) was a gardener. Then a cook. Then (subject.he/she) fell off a roof and learned to carve while (subject.he/she) healed. Then (subject.he/she) carved paddles, then canoes, then...

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells the whole winding story, with all the wrong turns. (friend) listens, increasingly amazed. "So none of it was planned?" "Not one bit." (friend) is quiet for a moment. "That makes me feel better, actually." (subject) laughs. "Good. You've got lots of wrong turns ahead of you. Some of them are the best part."
